REFERRED TO MENTAL HEALTH AND DEVELOPMENTAL DISABILITIES

items.actClause: AN ACT to amend the mental hygiene law, in relation to reimbursement of certain programs and services for persons with a disability
items.memo:
BILL NUMBER:S5544

TITLE OF BILL:

An act to amend the mental hygiene law, in relation to reimbursement of
certain programs and services for persons with a disability

PURPOSE:

To ensure local service providers are reimbursed from the Office for
People with Developmental Disabilities, for the rendering of approved
services, while such approval is pending.

SUMMARY OF PROVISIONS:

Section 1 amends § 13.15 of the mental hygiene law by adding a new
subdivision (c) to provide for the reimbursement of a service furnished
by a local service provider while the commissioner approves the service,
provided that such approval is ultimately granted.

Section 2 provides the effective date.

EXISTING LAW:

Pursuant to § 13.13 of the Mental Hygiene Law, local services for
persons with developmental disabilities shall be planned, financed, and
implemented in accordance with the provisions of this chapter.  Pursuant
to § 13.13 of the Mental Hygiene Law, the Commissioner of the Office for
People with Developmental Disabilities shall plan, promote, establish,
develop, coordinate, evaluate, and conduct programs and services of
prevention, diagnosis, examination, care, treatment, rehabilitation,
training, and research for the benefit of individuals with developmental
disabilities. Such programs shall include, but are not limited to, inpa-
tient, outpatient, partial hospitalization, day care, emergency, rehabi-
litative, and other appropriate treatments and services. The commission-
er shall take all actions necessary, desirable, or proper to implement
the purposes of this chapter, and to carry out the purposes and objec-
tives of the Office within the amounts made available therefore by
appropriation, grant, gift, devise, bequest, or allocation from the
Mental Health Service Fund established under § 97-f of the Finance Law.
The activities described here may be undertaken in cooperation and
agreement with other offices, departments, or agencies of the state,
local or federal government, or with other organizations and individ-
uals.

Pursuant to § 13.17(c) of the Mental Hygiene Law, the Commissioner of
the Office for People with Developmental Disabilities may authorize
other offices of the Department and any public or private non-profit
organization or political subdivision of the state to deliver supports
and services to individuals with development disabilities, not incon-
sistent with the programs and objectives of the Office in any facility
under the commissioner's jurisdiction. The commissioner may permit any

facility under the commissioner's jurisdiction to operate programs for
persons with mental disabilities, not inconsistent with programs and
objectives of the Department, under contracts or agreements with other
offices within the Department.

JUSTIFICATION:

Services rendered to persons with developmental disabilities by local
service providers and agencies must be approved the Office for Persons
with Developmental Disabilities (OPWDD). Generally, an individual, or a
family member on the behalf of an individual, will approach a local
service provider seeking disability services. That individual is then
referred to OPWDD for an evaluative process during which OPWDD will
determine the services that are available to the person and which
centers provide the approved services. A family may choose only from the
services and centers approved through OPWDD's assessment.

A local provider is proscribed from providing any service to a person
with a developmental disability until such service is approved by OPWDD.
Often, an initial placement in a particular program or the rendering of
specific services is inappropriate for the individual requiring the
service. This may result in extraordinary hardships for both the indi-
vidual and that person's caregivers, especially when the inappropriate
placement results in physical or emotional harm to the individual, or
when abridgement in service results in a lapse of day care thus forcing
the caregiver to modify his or her own employment obligations. Further-
more, local service providers cannot help facilitate the evaluation and
approval process and are prevented from advocating on behalf of their
clients and families.

In an effort to offer the necessary services and treatments to all of
their clients in a streamlined and consistent manner, local service
providers often provide uncompensated care. But uncompensated care does
not mean that the services provided were not approved by OPWDD.  Rather,
the uncompensated care may have been administered while the individual
was still being approved, or during an interim period when OPWDD had not
yet approved a more appropriate placement or treatment for that person's
particular needs.

This bill requires that if a person with developmental disabilities
qualifying for such a program and has entered into a program or received
a service furnished by a local service provider, and subsequently enters
into a different program or receives a different service not yet
approved by OPWDD, the local service provider must be reimbursed the
cost of that program or service as if it had been approved prior to such
person's admission to the program, provided that such approval is ulti-
mately granted by the Department. While only those services that are
ultimately approved by OPWDD quality for reimbursement during the inter-
im period, this bill will promote the consistent delivery of necessary
services to persons with developmental disabilities and ensure local
service providers are appropriately compensated for the rendering of
such approved services. This legislation will foster the relationship

between all of these parties, including individuals with developmental
disabilities and their families, local service providers, and OPWDD.  As
such it is imperative that this bill is enacted.

LEGISLATIVE HISTORY:

New Bill.

FISCAL IMPLICATIONS:

Minimal.

EFFECTIVE DATE:

This act shall take effect immediately.
